task.name: Delegated semantic adjudication: forge evaluates, adjudicates, remediates and retries agent-authored issues, escalating only what it cannot converge
task.story_text:
## Why

The v0.16.0 milestone is declared as "capture → shaped → groomed → ready without operator keystrokes; the operator decides commitments." The semantic review that was meant to close that chain was envisioned as the peer-review loop the operator had been running by hand: an agent drafts an issue from an observed defect or an operator idea, agents drift in prose and write broad or conflicting acceptance criteria, so a second agent reviews the draft, the author revises, and the reviewer approves. The operator sees only what the agents cannot converge.

What shipped (#2785, ADR-0009 clause 6) is a different system. The issue is admitted to a sprint as implementation-ready, sprint entry runs a reviewer, the sprint withholds the story, the operator reads the findings from the audit store, ratifies each one by hand (#2988 measured $0.46 outside `--budget` and one keystroke per issue per revision), edits the body, and restarts. A clean evaluation still needs an empty ratification. The operator became the integration layer between two agents, which is the work the feature was supposed to remove. #2988 turns the gate off by default so work can proceed; this spike decides the replacement.

Two design facts fall out of the measurement. First, the loop belongs in issue production, where the text is authored and changed, not at sprint admission, where the text is supposed to be settled. Second, the reviewer needs the context a manual reviewing agent gets: repository conventions, linked and dependency issues, and the provenance of mechanically generated sections. Two of #2988's three findings were false positives from a reviewer that saw only the body: a dependency declared transitively, and an "Independence note" the diagnosis renderer inserts.

This spike ends in an ADR amendment plus runnable implementation issue(s), or a recorded "don't do" with the measured reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- A design document amends ADR-0009 clause 6 so that the author-reviewer loop is a stage of issue production: `todo`, `shape`, `groom` and `diagnose` drive evaluation, adjudication, remediation and bounded re-review of the document they produce, and an operator ratification is one of two adjudication kinds rather than the only one. The record distinguishes the two kinds so an audit never reads a delegated adjudication as a human decision.
- Sprint admission consumes only the fact that an adjudicated review exists for the current revision digest. It does not run the reviewer, spend, or hand findings to the operator; a document whose review predates its current revision is returned to production, not withheld awaiting a keystroke.
- The policy states what completes without a keystroke: a revision whose review raises no concern, or whose concerns were all remediated and re-reviewed clean within the retry bound. It states the complete escalation list: an unresolved product or policy decision, reviewer disagreement with the author's stated intent, a review or remediation failure, and non-convergence at the retry ceiling. Anything outside the list has a stated default so an unclassified outcome cannot silently complete.
- Retries are bounded. The document names the ceiling and what happens at it, and no path re-reviews or re-remediates unboundedly.
- The reviewer is given the context a manual reviewing agent receives: the project's conventions, the issues the document links to or depends on, and which sections were generated mechanically. A finding against a mechanically generated section, or against a relationship visible in a linked issue, is a measured false-positive class the POC reports on.
- The policy is selectable per project. A project may require human ratification for all documents, and a project that does not still gets every review, adjudication, remediation and escalation recorded in the semantic-review store against the revision digest it was made against.
- The POC runs the loop end to end on at least three real agent-authored issues from a dogfood project and records, per issue: rounds to convergence, spend, whether it escalated and why, the false-positive count with and without context, and whether the operator agreed with the final state on inspection. The spike does not close without those numbers.
- The spike ends in one of two recorded outcomes: the ADR amendment merged plus runnable implementation issue(s) filed with `depends_on` this spike, or a documented decision not to proceed with the measured reason.

## Example

As shipped, rc18, an agent-authored enhancement:

```
groom 433           -> RUNNABLE
sprint --issues 433 -> evaluate: 3 concerns ($0.17, outside --budget)
                    -> withheld: semantic_review_not_ratified
(operator reads records.jsonl, decides three findings)
ratify-semantic 433 --accept a --accept b --accept c
(operator rewrites the body by hand)
sprint --issues 433 -> evaluate r2: 0 concerns -> withheld again
ratify-semantic 433
sprint --issues 433 -> admitted
```

Under the loop this spike proposes, the same issue never reaches the sprint unreviewed:

```
groom 433 --apply   -> r1 RUNNABLE
                       review r1 (with conventions, linked #429 #431, generated sections marked): 3 concerns
                       adjudicate: 3 fixable-in-body
                       revise     -> r2
                       review r2: 0 concerns
                       recorded: delegated adjudication, r2, 2 rounds, $0.31
                    -> READY
sprint --issues 433 -> review on record for r2 -> admitted
```

And one that reaches the operator:

```
groom 451 --apply   -> r1 RUNNABLE
                       review r1: 1 concern
                       adjudicate: product decision ("drop days or lower sets first?")
                    -> ESCALATED
forge status        -> #451 escalated: 1 product decision awaiting operator
```

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
